title: Which two digit number times eight fits the letters?
description: A two digit number with letters P Q is multiplied by eight to give another two digit number with letters R S. The video uses the size of the answer to cut the choices down to ten, eleven and twelve, then tests each one against the letter rules. Keeko doubts that ten will do, because the answer has two digits.
teaching_notes: One idea: use the size of the answer to list the possible numbers, then test each one against the rule that different letters hide different digits. Watch for students who stop at a choice that has the right number of digits without checking the letters.

video_script.why: The child knows multiplication facts, and now uses size and the rules of a letter puzzle to find hidden digits.
video_script.substitution: Bound the two digit number by the size of the answer, then test each choice against the rules.
video_script.anchor: the letter puzzle PQ × 8 = RS of the book, worked out by {{NAME_3}}
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko sees that 10 × 8 = 80 has two digits and says PQ is 10. Then Q and S are both 0, two letters for one digit, which the rules forbid.
video_script.payoff_line: P Q is twelve and R S is ninety six.

final_answer.spoken: P Q is twelve and R S is ninety six

names.{{NAME_3}}: the child who solves the cryptarithm PQ x 8 = RS

maths_rules: PQ × 8 = RS, with P, Q, R and S four different digits and P, R not 0
13 × 8 = 104 has three digits, and any bigger PQ gives more, so PQ is 10, 11 or 12
10 × 8 = 80: Q = 0 and S = 0, two letters for one digit, so 10 fails
11: P = 1 and Q = 1, two letters for one digit, so 11 fails (11 × 8 = 88 also repeats 8)
12 × 8 = 96: P = 1, Q = 2, R = 9, S = 6, all different, so 12 works
video_script.design: One puzzle PQ × 8 = RS. The choices ten, eleven and twelve are listed by size, then tested one by one against the letter rules.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='who'/>{{NAME_3}} looks at a letter puzzle, P Q times eight equals R S.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Each letter hides one digit, and different letters hide different digits.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What two digit number can P Q be?

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>P Q and R S are both two digit numbers, so P and R are not zero.
<bookmark mark='least'/>The smallest two digit number is ten, so the choices start there.
<bookmark mark='big'/>Eight times a number grows quickly, so the answer may soon get too big.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the digits of P Q and R S.

narration: <bookmark mark='size'/>Step one, find the biggest P Q, because R S has only two digits.
<bookmark mark='big'/>Thirteen times eight is one hundred and four, which has three digits.
<bookmark mark='list'/>Any bigger number gives an even bigger answer, so the choices are ten, eleven and twelve.

beats.on_screen: 10 × 8 = 80: the 0 of 10 and the 0 of 80 glow together, crossed; 11: P and Q are both 1, crossed

marks.test: the choices 10 and 11 are tested against the rule
marks.ten: 10 × 8 = 80 is written and the two zeros glow, crossed
marks.eleven: 11 is written with its two equal digits circled, crossed

beats.colours: the clashing digits in the warning colour
narration: <bookmark mark='test'/>Step two, test ten and eleven against the rules, because they may repeat a digit.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Ten times eight is eighty, and then Q and S are both zero.
<bookmark mark='eleven'/>Eleven has the same digit twice, but P and Q are different letters.
Neither choice works.

beats.on_screen: 12 × 8 = 96; the letters get their digits: P = 1, Q = 2, R = 9, S = 6; all four digits glow different

marks.map: the letters get their digits P = 1, Q = 2, R = 9, S = 6

narration: <bookmark mark='twelve'/>Step three, test twelve, the last choice left.
<bookmark mark='map'/>Twelve times eight is ninety six. Here P is one, Q is two, R is nine and S is six.
<bookmark mark='diff'/>The four digits are all different, so twelve fits every rule.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>P Q is twelve and R S is ninety six.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks P Q is ten, because ten times eight is eighty, which has two digits.
<bookmark mark='zeros'/>But then Q is zero and S is zero, so two letters hide one digit.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Different letters need different digits, so the right size is not enough. We must check the letters too.
